correctness.rationale: For binary adjacent multisets, the pair is determined by its sum, so the read distance is ordinary Hamming distance between eight-symbol sum vectors. The compatibility graph therefore has exactly the 128 binary words as vertices and codes are cliques. The bundled verifier proves the clique number by two exact searches, and a fresh independent branch-and-bound reconstruction in this audit again returned clique number \(8\). The displayed eight-word set was checked pairwise. The classical comparison follows independently from the radius-one Hamming bound and the length-seven Hamming code.
correctness.risk: The exhaustive proof establishes only this single finite parameter row.

value.rationale: This is a natural first perfect-Hamming-length benchmark for the distance-five \(2\)-read problem. The exact value demonstrates that the read-vector constraint costs a factor of two beyond the known classical-distance reduction, so the finite invariant is mathematically motivated and useful for calibrating general bounds.

final_claim: The maximum size of a binary zero-padded \(2\)-read length-seven code with read-vector Hamming distance at least \(5\) is exactly \(8\); an explicit eight-word code attains the bound, whereas the corresponding classical binary \((7,3)\) optimum is \(16\).
limitations: Exact only for binary alphabet, length seven, read length two, and minimum read distance five.
The exhaustive clique computation is finite and is not extrapolated to an infinite family.
